name: Hot Honey Chicken and Broccoli Bowls
intro_html: Sweet, a little spicy, and shockingly lean. Chicken breast and tender broccoli over rice, all glazed in hot honey for a sweet-heat kick that makes leftovers something to look forward to. At 31 grams of protein and only 3 grams of fat for around $2.12 a bowl (at everyday cost), this one earns a permanent spot in the rotation.
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb raw (1587 g)
Hot Honey (Better Goods): about 7 tbsp (7/16 cup) (147 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast, 3.5 lb raw: ~$7.80. Buy 4 lbs: $8.92.
Rice, 3.5 cups dry jasmine: ~$0.86. Buy 1 (lasts several batches).
Hot Honey, about 7 tbsp (7/16 cup): ~$2.14. Buy 1 (lasts several batches).
Olive Oil, ~2 tbsp (cook chicken/roast broccoli): ~$0.99. Buy 1 (lasts several batches).
Soy Sauce, 3 tbsp (in glaze): ~$0.34. Buy 1 (lasts several batches).
Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper): ~$0.14. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $14.72 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.05 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $16.18 across 14 servings, roughly $1.16 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $13.46 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $29.64. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $2.12 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a lean, crave-worthy dinner that would run $12 or more at a fast-casual spot.
shop_smart: Chicken on sale, frozen, is the move. Buy a big pack when the price drops and freeze it in two-pound bags.
A little hot honey goes far. One bottle glazes several batches, so the per-serving cost stays tiny even though it feels like a treat.
Frozen broccoli is cheaper than fresh, lasts for months, and cooks right from the bag.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice. Three and a half cups dry jasmine with water per the package, then set aside.
Cube the chicken, season it with the salt and black pepper, and cook in a large skillet with the olive oil over medium-high heat until it reaches 165F inside.
Steam or microwave the broccoli until bright and tender.
Turn the heat to low, stir the minced garlic into the chicken for a few seconds, then drizzle the hot honey and soy sauce over and toss until glazed.
Combine the rice, hot honey chicken, and broccoli in your big pot and stir.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty-pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and scoop the exact amount into each container. Every bowl lands near 357 calories and 31 grams of protein at just 3 grams of fat.
upsell_html: Lean, crave-worthy dinners for about $2.12 a bowl (at everyday cost). This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

head.description: A lean sweet-and-spicy chicken, broccoli, and rice meal prep glazed in hot honey. Fourteen servings at about 357 calories, 31 grams of protein, and only 3 grams of fat for roughly $2.12 each (at everyday cost).

recipeIngredient: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast, 3.5 lb raw (1587 g)
Hot Honey, about 7 tbsp (7/16 cup) (147 g)
Olive Oil, ~2 tbsp (cook chicken/roast broccoli) (100 g)
steps: Cook 3.5 cups dry jasmine rice per the package and set aside.
Season the cubed chicken with salt and black pepper and cook it in the olive oil until it reaches 165F.
Steam or microwave the broccoli until tender.
Lower the heat, add the minced garlic, then drizzle the hot honey and soy sauce over and toss to glaze.
Combine rice, chicken, and broccoli and stir.
Weigh the batch and divide into 14 containers.
